body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「一個虛構嘅供應商支援 workflow 透過 MCP server 搵到 `send_supplier_message` 工具。Agent 已經產生咗格式正確嘅 recipient、subject 同 body。你會點樣設計 integration，確保『搵到工具』永遠唔會變成『獲准發送』？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「喺 tool metadata 標記佢有後果，再喺 chat 放一個確認掣；user 一按 Confirm，agent 就可以 call 呢個工具。」

## MCP 在呢度負責乜

呢題入面，MCP 只係讓 agent host 發現一個遠端工具，知道佢收乜欄位，並在需要時提出 call 嘅通道。呢啲資料講嘅係 capability：server 提供乜嘢。佢唔會講清邊個目前有權代表哪個 tenant、向哪個供應商、用邊個內容發送訊息。就算 metadata 有提示一個 tool 可能有副作用，提示都只可以幫 host 決定點樣呈現或預設收窄；佢唔係 authorization。

好似餐牌列出有送餐服務，唔等於坐低嘅任何一個人都可以叫餐廳用任何地址送出任何一份餐。Tool discovery 係餐牌；approval 係有人核對地址、內容、付款責任同確實落單。將兩樣混埋，model 只要產生一次睇落合理嘅 call，就可能越過本來要由人作出嘅決定。

## 先將「想做」變成可核對嘅 proposal

Host 收到 tool list 後，先由自己嘅 policy 將每個操作分成 read、draft、proposal 或 consequential action。`send_supplier_message` 唔應該直接出現喺 model 可執行嘅 path；第一步只可以建立一份 proposal。Proposal 要有虛構個案 ID、受影響供應商、指定 sender profile、recipient、subject、body 的 digest、預期效果、原因、policy version、建立人同到期時間。

Reviewer 睇到嘅應該係一個可讀嘅差異：訊息會去邊個地址、會講乜、點解要而家發、同上一次已批版本有冇改過，而唔係一粒模糊嘅「Sure?」按鈕。呢個流程亦要有 non-technical owner：哪一類 supplier escalation 由誰決定可發，甚麼情況必須交返採購或 support，失敗後由誰跟進。Model 可以幫手起草理由；佢唔可以自己寫 `approved: true`。

## Approval 要同真正要發生嘅事綁定

批核後，backend 建立一個短時效 approval record 或 grant，綁定 proposal digest、action、tenant、target、policy version 同 idempotency key。Idempotency key 即係同一宗已獲批嘅動作重送幾次，都只可以有一個可追查結果。真正發送前，action adapter 再檢查 grant、目前身份、目標、內容 digest、時效同重送情況。recipient 或 body 改一個字、policy 更新、或者 grant 過期，都要回到 approval，而唔係沿用舊 token。

如果 MCP server 由你控制，呢啲檢查應該由 server 做；如果係第三方 integration，就喺你控制嘅 adapter 或 policy service 前面做，唔好只靠 chat modal。無論控制擺邊，model text、tool annotation 同 client-side button 都唔可以係最後一道門。結果亦要由服務端 receipt 決定。timeout 或未知結果時，UI 應該顯示 `unknown / reconcile`，而唔係因為 model 講咗「已發送」就當完成。

## 測試要搵到繞過 UI 嘅路

最小 fixture set 唔係得一宗順利發送。至少包括：metadata 缺少或錯誤描述副作用時，policy 仍然唔會 default allow；agent 嘗試直接 call send tool 時只得到 draft 或 handoff；approval 係 A，但發送前 recipient 改成 B；body digest、tenant、role 或 policy version 不相符；grant 已過期；有人繞過 UI 直接 request action adapter；同一 idempotency key 被 retry；下游接受咗 request 但 response timeout。

每個 case 都要寫 expected state：`draft`、`awaiting_approval`、`denied`、`executed` 或 `unknown_reconcile`。最重要嘅否定證據係：格式正確嘅 MCP call，喺冇有效 grant 時仍然無法做出外部效果。咁先分得清係模型提議有問題、policy 拒絕咗、定係 integration 真的有不確定結果。

## 留畀 reviewer 睇嘅嘢

- **工程記錄：** `fixtures/mcp-tool-list.json`、action classification table、proposal schema、approval-grant verifier，同埋 cover 變更內容、過期、bypass 同 duplicate 嘅 tests。
- **工作流程記錄：** 一頁 decision record，列清 fictitious workflow 的 decision owner、準許的 sender scope、handoff 條件、revoke path 同未知結果由誰對帳。
- **不應該放大嘅聲稱：** 呢套 fixture 證明本地規則點樣 route case，唔證明任何真實供應商帳戶已連接、訊息已送達、policy 已獲安全或法律批准，亦唔證明節省時間或改善業務結果。

## 延伸閱讀

[Tool schema 唔等於最小權限](/zh-HK/interview-lab/tool-schema-is-not-least-privilege)、[Agent draft 不作有後果 action](/zh-HK/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions) 同 [將 approval queue 做成可核對嘅 portfolio evidence](/zh-HK/articles/approval-queue-low-code-portfolio)。

## 範圍說明

呢個係 AI.DOG 單題練習。MCP server、供應商、訊息、身份、grant、receipt 同測試結果都係虛構或 synthetic local fixture。佢唔會連接帳戶、發送訊息、建立真實授權，亦唔代表任何公司嘅現時 integration、面試流程或 production control。

> 面試官問：「一個虛構的供應商支援 workflow 透過 MCP server 找到 `send_supplier_message` 工具。Agent 已產生格式正確的 recipient、subject 與 body。你會怎麼設計 integration，確保『找到工具』永遠不會變成『獲准發送』？」
>
> 答對一半的回答：「在 tool metadata 標示它會造成後果，再在 chat 放一個確認按鈕；user 按 Confirm 後，agent 就可以 call 這個工具。」

在這題裡，MCP 只是讓 agent host 發現遠端工具、知道它接收哪些欄位，並在需要時提出 call 的通道。這些資料說的是 capability：server 提供什麼。它不會說明誰目前有權代表哪個 tenant、向哪個供應商、用哪一段內容發送訊息。即使 metadata 有提示某個 tool 可能有副作用，提示也只能幫 host 決定如何呈現或預設收窄；它不是 authorization。

就像菜單列有外送服務，不代表坐下來的任何人都可以叫餐廳把任何一份餐送到任何地址。Tool discovery 是菜單；approval 是有人核對地址、內容、付款責任並確實下單。把兩件事混在一起，model 只要產生一次看似合理的 call，就可能跨過原本該由人作出的決策。

核准後，backend 建立短時效 approval record 或 grant，綁定 proposal digest、action、tenant、target、policy version 與 idempotency key。Idempotency key 的意思是同一項已核准動作重送多次，也只能有一個可追查結果。真正發送前，action adapter 再檢查 grant、目前身分、目標、內容 digest、時效與重送狀況。recipient 或 body 改一個字、policy 更新，或 grant 過期，都要回到 approval，而不能沿用舊 token。

## 留給 reviewer 檢查的東西

- **工程記錄：** `fixtures/mcp-tool-list.json`、action classification table、proposal schema、approval-grant verifier，以及涵蓋內容變更、過期、bypass 與 duplicate 的 tests。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 单题练习。MCP server、供应商、消息、身份、grant、receipt 和测试结果都是虚构或 synthetic local fixture。它不会连接账户、发送消息、建立真实授权，也不代表任何公司的当前 integration、面试流程或 production control。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “A fictional supplier-support workflow discovers a `send_supplier_message` tool through an MCP server. The agent has generated a well-formed recipient, subject, and body. How would you design the integration so discovering the tool never becomes permission to send?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Mark the tool as consequential in its metadata and put a confirmation button in the chat. Once the user clicks Confirm, the agent can call it.”

## What MCP does here

In this question, MCP is only the connection through which an agent host discovers a remote tool, learns its fields, and can propose a call. That information describes capability: what the server offers. It does not say who may currently act for which tenant, which supplier, or which message content. Even when metadata hints that a tool may have side effects, that hint can help a host present or narrow the tool. It is not authorisation.

A menu that lists delivery is not a signed instruction to send any meal to any address. Tool discovery is the menu. Approval is somebody checking the address, content, responsibility, and actual order. If those are treated as one thing, a plausible-looking model call can cross a decision that was meant to belong to a person.

## Turn intent into a checkable proposal

After receiving a tool list, the host should use its own policy to classify each operation as read, draft, proposal, or consequential action. `send_supplier_message` should not appear on a model-executable path. Its first possible outcome is a proposal. That proposal records a fictional case ID, affected supplier, named sender profile, recipient, subject, a digest of the body, intended effect, reason, policy version, creator, and expiry.

A reviewer should see a readable difference: where the message will go, what it will say, why it should be sent now, and whether it changed since the last approved version. That is more useful than a vague “Sure?” button. The workflow also needs a non-technical owner: who decides that a kind of supplier escalation may be sent, when it goes back to procurement or support, and who follows up after failure. The model may draft a reason; it cannot set `approved: true` for itself.

## Bind approval to the thing that will happen

After review, the backend creates a short-lived approval record or grant bound to the proposal digest, action, tenant, target, policy version, and idempotency key. An idempotency key means repeat delivery of the same approved action produces one traceable result, rather than several sends. Before delivery, an action adapter checks the grant, current principal, target, content digest, expiry, and replay status again. A one-character recipient or body change, a policy update, or an expired grant returns the work to approval rather than reusing an old token.

If you own the MCP server, enforce those checks there. If the integration is third party, put an adapter or policy service you control before consequential execution. In either case, model text, tool annotations, and a client-side button cannot be the final gate. A server-side receipt decides the result. When a timeout leaves delivery unknown, the UI should say `unknown / reconcile`, not treat “sent” in model prose as completion.

## Test the route that bypasses the UI

A useful fixture set contains more than one successful send. Include metadata that omits or misstates side effects, while policy still refuses to default-allow; an agent that tries to call the send tool directly and receives only a draft or handoff; approval for A followed by recipient B; mismatched body digest, tenant, role, or policy version; an expired grant; a direct request to the action adapter that bypasses the UI; a retry with the same idempotency key; and a downstream acceptance followed by response timeout.

Give every case an expected state: `draft`, `awaiting_approval`, `denied`, `executed`, or `unknown_reconcile`. The most valuable negative proof is a well-formed MCP call that still cannot create an external effect without a valid grant. It separates a bad model proposal, a policy denial, and a genuinely uncertain integration result.

## What a reviewer can inspect

- **Engineering record:** `fixtures/mcp-tool-list.json`, an action-classification table, proposal schema, approval-grant verifier, and tests for content change, expiry, bypass, and duplicate delivery.
- **Workflow record:** a one-page decision record naming the fictional workflow's decision owner, allowed sender scope, handoff condition, revoke path, and who reconciles an unknown result.
- **Claims not to inflate:** these fixtures show how local rules route cases. They do not show a real supplier account, a delivered message, a security or legal approval, saved time, or better business outcomes.

## Further reading

[A tool schema is not least privilege](/en/interview-lab/tool-schema-is-not-least-privilege), [Let an agent draft without consequential actions](/en/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions), and [make an approval queue inspectable portfolio evidence](/en/articles/approval-queue-low-code-portfolio).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. The MCP server, suppliers, messages, identities, grants, receipts, and test results are fictional or synthetic local fixtures. It does not connect an account, send a message, create real authority, or represent any company’s current integration, interview process, or production control.
